items.title: Ernie Cagnolatti Interview, 1961-04-05
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Do most trumpet players play with your lips wet? I never think about that, Arden. I never played drumming to start with.

ctx.x: No, he was more in favor of playing with your lips wet, see. That moist lips keep from cracking. You see, dry lips, what actually happens, I could say it in a lot of time, your throat gets dry too. And your mouthpiece, nine out of ten, will stick to your lip. And if you move it, well, you slip off your armature, you see. Where they're wet, they're not going to slip off your armature. All you would have to leave your lips stay wet and just wipe their mouthpiece off and put it right back, see. And it'll fall right…
Do most trumpet players play with their lips wet? I never think about that, Arden. I never played drumming to start with.
I think the majority of them do. I mean, it looks like it comes natural to them. It just comes natural to them.
